# XDR403: error or ok result discarded on a value that is then stored

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | XDR4xx: assumptions about the ledger's form, ranges and outcomes |
| How to fix | check the error (or ok) and fail or skip the row with a logged reason; a zero value stored in its place is indistinguishable from a real one |
| Default severity | warning (`severity: {XDR403: …}` changes it) |
| Default rule set | yes |
| Guide | [Validated versus unvalidated fields](../../guide/indexer-hardening.mdx#validated-fields) |
| Self-audit checklist item | HC-108 |
| Demonstrating corpus entry | `cap-0067/address-types-in-sac-events-golden` (registered in [corpus/plan.json](../../corpus/plan.json)) |
| Fixtures | [lint/testdata/xdr4xx/xdr403](../testdata/xdr4xx/xdr403) |

## What it reports

`v, _ := f(…)`, where `f` returns an error as its last result and is a function of the SDK module (`xdr`,
`strkey`, `amount`, `ingest`, `processors`, …), `strconv`, `encoding/hex`, `encoding/base64`, `encoding/json`,
`math/big` or `time` (or is `big.Int.SetString`, with its ok result), and `v` is later stored in the same
function: part of a composite literal, assigned to a field, map entry or slice element, appended, or passed to a
database call or a builder. A variable tested in a condition first (`if v == "" { … }`) counts as checked.

Not reported: `strkey.Encode` of a 32-byte array (an ID; it cannot fail), and a parse of a string field of an SDK
struct (the SDK formatted it).

## Why it matters

A discarded error leaves the zero value in its place: an empty address, amount 0, a zero ID. Stored, it cannot be
told apart from a real value, and nothing records that the row is wrong.

## Example

Reported:

```go
// lint/testdata/xdr4xx/xdr403/bad.go
// (b) An amount that did not parse is stored as 0.
func amount(s string, row *transferRow) {
	f, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
	row.Amount = f
}
```

Not reported:

```go
// lint/testdata/xdr4xx/xdr403/good.go
func destinationChecked(id xdr.Hash) (transferRow, error) {
	to, err := strkey.Encode(strkey.VersionByteContract, id[:])
	if err != nil {
		return transferRow{}, err
	}
	return transferRow{To: to}, nil
}
```

## Limits

A discarded `ok` of an xdr `Get<Arm>()` accessor is not reported: one wide row per union, with the other arms left
at zero, is a common and deliberate layout (XDR105 covers arm reads that panic). Uses in another function are not
followed.

## Configure and suppress

Turn the rule off by leaving XDR403 out of `rules` in `.xdrlint.yml` or a profile. To accept one report, put `//xdrlint:ignore XDR403 <reason>` on the reported line or on the enclosing function's doc comment (under golangci-lint, `//nolint:xdrlint // <reason>`), or add an entry to an external suppression file for code you cannot edit. A suppression needs a reason, and one that suppresses nothing is itself reported (XDR000). See [Configuring and suppressing](README.md#linter-suppressions).
